title: Derived completeness of finite constant scalar local models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_F$ with its induced $\ell$-adic norm topology, and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$, put $B_T=p_T^*\underline A$ and $k_{n,T}=(A/\pi^n)_T$ for $n\ge1$. Use the small pro-étale sites and universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the ordinary unbounded derived module categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $C_T(K)=R\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{B_T}k_{n,T})$ and $c_{T,K}:K\to C_T(K)$ for the specified strict-tower completion unit [sk-def-pe-derived-completion, lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison].
Let $T$ be any scheme and $M$ a $B_T$-module sheaf with a finite constant scalar local model [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there is a pro-étale cover $\{U_i\to T\}$ and finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P_i$ with $M|_{U_i}\simeq B_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{P_i}$, where finitely presented means a cokernel of a map between finite free $A$-modules, and underlines on scalar modules mean constant sheaves. Then $c_{T,M[0]}$ is an isomorphism.
In particular this holds for every global scalar model $B_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline P$, including torsion $P$, and for every finite power $B_T^d$, $d\ge0$. For the free case the canonical cone-to-quotient maps identify the strict reduction tower of $B_T^d[0]$ with $(k_{n,T}^d[0])_n$, compatibly with the actual quotient transitions and augmentations. The isomorphism $B_T^d[0]\simeq R\varprojlim_n k_{n,T}^d[0]$ so obtained carries the completion unit to the inverse-limit cone with its specified scalar quotient projections. No geometric condition on $T$ or torsion-freeness of the scalar modules is assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing coefficient short exact sequence of the completion-triangle comparison, map it by the d-fold biproduct and then by the degree-zero single functor. Naturality of scalar action identifies its first arrow with the actual principal scalar on the finite free complex. The mapping-cone short-exact comparison gives the map from each canonical principal cone to the actual finite quotient power. Its formula is zero on the shifted summand and quotient on the unshifted summand. The canonical transition and augmentation coordinate equations prove that these maps form one strict tower morphism, with all the required coordinates.

source.place: Local models; free case, with the normalized strict principal quotient resolution

proof.text: The integral coefficient quotient cone is limiting and its transitions are epi. Finite biproduct powers preserve limits, as does the degree-zero single functor. Hence the finite-free quotient cone is limiting with exactly its specified projections. The generic Roos kernel calculation identifies its inclusion as the kernel of one minus the product shift. The pro-etale tower epimorphism theorem makes that difference map degreewise epi. The degreewise-epi kernel-to-shifted-cone comparison shows that the quotient augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The Roos calculus carries the strict tower map of Step 1 to a quasi-isomorphism. Its coordinate formula identifies every specified strict completion augmentation with this quotient augmentation after that same tower map. The completion-triangle comparison therefore makes the free completion unit invertible, including rank zero.

source.place: Propositions 3.1.9--3.1.10; the strict augmented comparison uses the existing principal/Roos normalization nodes

proof.text: Apply the existing two-term free resolution of a finitely presented ordinary scalar module. Its two free terms are complete by Step 2. The short exact sequence supplies its degree-zero distinguished triangle. The exact completion functor and its natural unit give a morphism to the completed distinguished triangle; two-out-of-three makes the final unit invertible. This proves completeness for each ordinary scalar presentation, including torsion modules.

source.place: Local models, exact length-one scalar resolution; completion-unit triangle argument from Bhatt--Scholze Section 3.4

proof.text: Use the existing normalized strict completion restriction comparison for each weakly-etale map in a pro-etale model cover. Its derived comparison is an isomorphism and its unit equation identifies the restricted original unit with the completion unit of the restricted object. The comparison concerns these covering slices and preserves the specified augmentation.

source.place: Section 3.4, paragraph following Definition 3.4.1: restriction commutes with homotopy limits; strict-unit refinement using the displayed principal and Roos formulas

proof.text: Use the existing local-model representative theorem to express each model chart by an actual finite scalar matrix cokernel. Transport between the two coefficient topology presentations using equality of the induced topologies. Over the scalar DVR these matrix cokernels are finitely presented, so Step 3 applies. The derived inverse-image factorization and single-functor comparison transport completeness through the chart isomorphism. Step 4 and joint conservativity on a pro-etale cover show that the original completion unit is invertible. A global condensed-point finite presentation is a local model using the identity cover and the pullback composition comparison.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-bbcf2327e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all 5 steps, all 6 stmt_deps and 18 proof_deps, blueprint ctf-equals-bc.proof (Local models, Locality) and Bhatt-Scholze Props 3.1.9-3.1.10 and the paragraph after Def 3.4.1. The delivery has no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, an ancestry check over 1485 nodes finds no cycle, no SGA is cited, and there is no re-split note. Step 1: flatness and B/pi^n=k_n (integral criterion), DVR, and the flat cyclic resolution give injectivity of pi^n. The cone-to-cokernel map is a quasi-isomorphism. I checked by hand that the transition (x,y)->(x,pi y) is a chain map and is compatible with q_n and j_n. Step 2: on a degree-0 surjective tower the Roos complex is [prod -> prod] with kernel lim and cokernel 0. H(q) sends c=(((m,0))_n,0) to ((m mod pi^n)_n,0). B^d->lim k_n^d is the canonical iso, and its projections are the quotient maps (one-line check). So the free unit is an isomorphism with the stated normalisation. Step 3: the finite-flat resolution over a flat DVR algebra (torsion P allowed), the completion morphism of triangles including the last square, and two-of-three. Step 4: slice restriction is exact, products are sectionwise and F|U(V/U)=F(V), so restriction commutes literally with D_n, Roos and c. alpha_u is natural in the coefficient ring, so it respects pi. The step avoids any claim that arbitrary inverse images preserve products. Step 5: naturality of c plus conservativity on covers for any condensed ring and any cover. Edge cases checked: T empty, d=0, P=0, P=A/pi^r (H^-1 handled through the resolution), n=1, infinite covers. All 18 tool_uses are accepted as generic coefficient, completion and site tools. Duplicate search (rg -L for derived complete with local/scalar model): candidates are perfect-model, line, cohomology-only or Noetherian variants, none a duplicate. Maintainer note: the same-day unsplit sibling lem-sfb-strict-completion-restriction-comparison contains the site-object case of Step 4. I kept the inline proof because it rests only on reviewed nodes, while the sibling also asserts product preservation for locally closed immersions. The sibling can reuse Step 4's argument when it is split. Advisory: the item names module-object categories while the tools use section-ring module sheaves, which the DAG's E_T equivalence identifies without changing sheaves, sections or morphisms. No fixes written.

lean.statement: theorem finite_scalar_local_model_complete : (∀ M : Modules l E T, HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) T M → IsDerivedComplete l E T (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((singleFunctor (Modules l E T) 0).obj M))) ∧ (∀ P : Mod (Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}) (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E), Mod.IsFinitelyPresented (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) P → IsDerivedComplete l E T (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((singleFunctor (Modules l E T) 0).obj ((DerivedNakayama.pullback l E T).obj P)))) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, IsDerivedComplete l E T (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (freeComplex l E T d)) ∧ ∀ data : PrincipalReductionConeData l E T, data.IsCanonical l E T → ∃ (q : (CompletionTriangle.tower l E T data).obj (freeComplex l E T d) ⟶ quotientTower l E T d) (b : freeComplex l E T d ⟶ roosF.obj (quotientTower l E T d)) (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (freeComplex l E T d) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (roosF.obj (quotientTower l E T d))), (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso ((HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map q).app (op n))) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ), (q.f k).app (op n) = (data.χ n (freeComplex l E T d) k).hom ≫ biprod.fst ≫ (quotientChainMap l E T d n).f k) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (data.j n).app (freeComplex l E T d) ≫ (HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map q).app (op n) = quotientChainMap l E T d n) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, b.f (p + 1) ≫ (roosχ (quotientTower l E T d) p).hom = biprod.lift 0 ((Pi.lift (fun n : ℕ ↦ quotientChainMap l E T d n)).f (p + 1))) ∧ e.hom = DerivedCategory.Q.map b ∧ (∀ a : 𝟭 (CochainComplex (Modules l E T) ℤ) ⟶ CompletionTriangle.complexCompletion l E T data, (∀ p : ℤ, (a.app (freeComplex l E T d)).f (p + 1) ≫ (roosχ ((CompletionTriangle.tower l E T data).obj (freeComplex l E T d)) p).hom = biprod.lift 0 ((Pi.lift (f := fun n : ℕ ↦ ((CompletionTriangle.tower l E T data).obj (freeComplex l E T d)).asFunctor.obj (op n)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ (data.j n).app (freeComplex l E T d))).f (p + 1))) → a.app (freeComplex l E T d) ≫ roosF.map q = b))
lean.note: The theorem jointly states local, global scalar-presentation, and finite-free completeness, with an augmented strict cone-to-quotient tower quasi-isomorphism and a unit-normalized derived isomorphism. Global scalar presentations use the same condensed-point finite-matrix encoding as the recorded constructibility dependency. Helpers are actual finite powers and actual quotient maps, not new independent notions.
